discussion_comments.comment_body:
This is a messy part, finding the environment variables relating to the current `.parse()` call. This will mostly work fine. In practice, normally will be on the program. 

However, technically possible to call `.parse()` directly on a subcommand too. So a call to parse on one level, then a call to parse on another level, may see stale state. Not a normal situation.

Would be more robust if cleared env in `.restoreStateBeforeParse()` so does not rely on being overwritten by subsequent call on _same_ command as the previous call.
I would prefer to have the `process.type` test in the `electron` handling. So for example, user can potentially specify `from: "electron"` and get the full logic.
One of the features of the config helper is it handles whether the config is an object or an array of objects, and likewise for the `extends`, so removed the spread operator.
